subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Fukushima: When Nature Exceeds Design
description: A quick, practical guide to Fukushima: When Nature Exceeds Design.

hook.text: On March 11, 2011, a 15-meter tsunami hit Fukushima Daiichi. The seawall was designed for 5.7 meters.

buildup.text: The earthquake triggered automatic reactor shutdown — as designed. But the tsunami flooded the backup diesel generators.

discovery.text: Without power, cooling pumps stopped. Reactor fuel overheated, melting through containment. Three reactors suffered meltdowns.

twist.text: TEPCO had evidence of larger historical tsunamis but didn't raise the seawall. Cost and schedule pressures won.

climax.text: Japan shut down all 54 reactors for review. New global standards require protection against beyond-design-basis events.

punchline.text: The earthquake was survived. The wave was not planned for.

quiz.question: Why did Fukushima's backup systems fail during the tsunami?
options: The earthquake damaged the backup generators before the tsunami arrived
The tsunami flooded basement diesel generators that powered the cooling pumps
Operators couldn't access the control room due to radiation levels
